newsitem.title: GERMANY: Strauss-Kahn sees agreement on EMU pact-German TV.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn sees agreement on EMU pact-German TV.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn expects to reach agreement at the EU summit on Monday on a stability pact for monetary union and on employment strategy, Germany's ZDF television channel reported.

"We might have a text on Sunday evening, but perhaps not. In any case we will find a solution on Monday," ZDF quoted Strauss-Kahn as saying, in an advance release of an interview to be aired later on Sunday.

The French finance minister was referring to efforts to ratify the stability pact, which is designed to ensure fiscal discipline under the euro, and to efforts to agree a European strategy on jobs, ZDF said.
Strauss-Kahn also said that a European union agreement on job creation would neither involve additional funds nor a changed role for the future European Central Bank.

"The European Central Bank is as it should be and nothing will be changed in this regard. It is not a problem with the bank, nor is it a money problem. The problem is that we wish to have employment and growth a little explained," he said.
"And we want not to only talk about state funds or currency, but also about employement and growth," he added.
European Union leaders are arriving in Amsterdam this afternoon ahead of a two-day meeting that is supposed to culminate in agreement of a new treaty setting Europe's course for the new century.

However France stunned its partners last week by saying it wanted more time to study the stability pact, a German-initiated framework for keeping EU budgets in line after the introduction of the single currency in January, 1999.
